name: Rumination Disorder

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: DSM-5 Diagnostic Criteria for Rumination Disorder

criteria.description: Repeated regurgitation of food over a period of at least 1 month
Regurgitation is not preceded by nausea or associated with retching
Behavior is not attributable to an associated gastrointestinal or medical condition
Behavior does not occur exclusively during the course of anorexia nervosa, bulimia nervosa, or avoidant/restrictive food intake disorder

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: All three major criteria must be met for diagnosis
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of other medical and psychiatric causes of regurgitation

pathognomonic.symptomName: Repeated effortless regurgitation of recently ingested food
searchTerms: recently eaten food returns to mouth

pathognomonic.symptomName: Rechewing and reswallowing or spitting out regurgitated food
searchTerms: chewing and swallowing regurgitated food again

common.symptomName: Absence of nausea or retching prior to regurgitation
searchTerms: no nausea before food comes up

common.symptomName: Weight loss or failure to gain weight (especially in infants and children)
searchTerms: weight loss or failure to grow

occasional.symptomName: Social withdrawal or embarrassment related to symptoms
searchTerms: avoiding social situations due to symptoms
pneumonia caused by food entering lungs
imbalanced body salts due to vomiting

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests; possible electrolyte abnormalities if severe
imaging: Upper GI series may show normal anatomy
other: Observation of regurgitation behavior during clinical evaluation

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of heartburn and acid regurgitation
Regurgitation preceded by nausea or retching
Self-induced vomiting with intent to control weight
Avoidance or restriction of food intake without regurgitation
Often associated with sensory aversion or fear of aversive consequences

redFlags: Unexplained weight loss or failure to thrive
Presence of vomiting with nausea or retching
references: American Psychiatric Association. Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, 5th Edition (DSM-5). 2013.
Klein, M.D., et al. Rumination Syndrome: Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prognosis. Gastroenterology Clinics of North America. 2018.
Chial, H.J., et al. Rumination syndrome in children and adolescents. Journal of Pediatric Gastroenterology and Nutrition. 2003.
